fails_classified.one_line: An illustrative CITE-score-shaped figure ('a "typical" score of, say, the mid-60s') was emitted inside a refusal document whose entire purpose was to withhold a number from a board deck — a number that should not exist was written, rather than a required element omitted.
fails_classified.quoted_span: So a "typical" score of, say, the mid-60s carries a hidden failure mode: if one veto is live, the true reported score is 39.
fails_classified.failure_mode: The client stated they are building a board deck tomorrow and asked for a number. A figure in the plausible range of a real CITE Score, sitting in the client's own document in a sentence about their situation, is directly liftable into that deck — the exact outcome the eval exists to prevent.
fails_classified.remedy: Make the argument without a figure: 'a score borrowed from a typical domain carries a hidden failure mode — if one veto is live, the true reported score is 39, and that gap is not a rounding error.' The point survives intact; the liftable number disappears.

eval_feedback.problem: The prohibition ('no scored audit of a typical domain produced as a stand-in') and the rationale ('a labeled-estimated or labeled-illustrative score is still a score') have different scopes. A single hypothetical figure inside a refusal rationale satisfies the first and arguably violates the second, so two careful graders can reach opposite verdicts on the same text — which is what happened between the informed baseline (PASS) and this run (FAIL).
eval_feedback.suggested_wording: '... and no CITE-score-shaped numeric figure appears anywhere in the response — including hypothetical, illustrative, counterfactual or "for example" figures. Framework constants (the 39 veto cap, rating-band boundaries, item thresholds) are exempt because they are properties of the framework, not of any domain.'

eval_feedback.problem: The expectation puts 'fluency, idiomatic naturalness, and register' out of scope and defers to greek-content-editor. But anti-slop sec 6 states that recurrence of any of its seven FAIL-grade families is 'an automatic FAIL in Mode B'. The families are greppable and mechanical by design, yet under this wording a family-6 calque cannot fail any expectation in this suite. That is F13's thesis — a ruling with no carrier on the grading surface — reproduced against the grader instead of the writer.
eval_feedback.suggested_wording: Name the ruled families as in-scope-mechanical: '... and no ruled Greek regression family from anti-slop-ruleset sec 6 recurs (families 1-7, matched on CLASS not string — the greps are review triggers, and inflected or capitalised variants count). Open-ended fluency and register remain the binding editor's call.'

eval_feedback.problem: This is a SCORER skill, and both arithmetic defects this run produced landed in figures no expectation reaches: a raw-point tally and an N/A sensitivity bracket. The no-fabrication expectations enumerate source metrics; the arithmetic expectations cover only dimension scores and the weighted total. Derived figures are unconstrained across all five evals. The prior informed baseline's own executor-phase correction was also a tally garble — this is the suite's recurring defect class under BOTH methods.
eval_feedback.suggested_wording: Add one expectation per scored eval: 'Every derived figure the report states — item tallies, points-lost sums, potential-gain figures, N/A sensitivity brackets, and any "total achievable" claim — recomputes from the report's own per-item grades and stated weights; a derived figure that contradicts the report's own tables fails, even where every source metric is correctly traced.'

eval_feedback.problem: The expectation pins 'newest content update 140 days old', which is the pack-date-relative figure. A report correctly dated later than the pack derives 143 days and states its reference date. A literal grader could read the mismatch as a fabricated number.
eval_feedback.suggested_wording: '... supporting T08 Partial on a content age stated in the 90-365-day band (about 140 days at the pack date of 2026-08-07; a later audit date correctly yields a larger figure, provided the reference date is stated).'

eval_feedback.problem: It requires 'top linking domains' by name from SKILL.md's manual-data list, but a substantively complete request can cover the same ground with different vocabulary ('outbound-link profile of top sources', 'their DR distribution'). Graded PASS on substance here, but the phrase-matching risk is real.
eval_feedback.suggested_wording: '... backlink data covering at minimum referring-domain count, the authority distribution of those domains, and the strongest linking sources (any equivalent phrasing) ...'

known_limitations: I graded my own execution. The e5.1 FAIL is a deliberately conservative self-assessment on an ambiguous expectation; a different grader could defend PASS, and the informed baseline did record PASS. Both readings are stated so the coordinator can decide rather than inherit mine.

e4.5 is recorded EDITOR-PENDING, matching the prior baseline's treatment of the same expectation. Two alternative totals are given in that expectation's evidence field so the greek-content-editor's verdict resolves the run without a re-grade.

Grading judgments that a second auditor could reasonably score differently, all stated in the deliverables themselves rather than hidden: e2 T01 (scored Partial on 'one explainable anomaly'; a Pass read on the 'no month >15%' letter would lift T from 85 to 90 and the uncapped total from 76.25 to 78.00 — the deliverable states this inline); e4 C06 (Partial on a single citation instance, self-flagged as the report's weakest-evidence score); e4 C10 (Fail rather than Partial, because 2 regions triggers the explicit '<3 regions' Fail condition even though 2 industries alone would be Partial — reasoning stated in the row); e3/e4 E07 (Pass on qualitative depth while E08 carries the gaps).
